raquel: Raquel — one of the two Jewish moneylenders of Burgos who take the pawned chests
a: a — to, at · also aver — he/she has (3rd sg. present, h-less spelling of ha, as in el rey me a ayrado = el rey me ha airado)
mio: mio — my (unstressed possessive; mio Çid 'my lord Cid')
çid: Çid — the Cid, 'lord' (Arabic sīdī 'my lord'; pronounced Tsid)
ha: aver — he has (3rd sg. present; = ha)
ya: ya — O! (vocative particle, Arabic yā); also 'now, already'
canpeador: Campeador — spelling variant with n for m (copyist's spelling) of Campeador, the Cid's epithet
buena: bueno — good (fem.); en buen(a) '(born/girded) in a good hour' — the poem's honorific formula
las: el/la — the (fem. pl.); them (fem. object pronoun)
yentes: yente — people, folk (= gente; y- from Latin g-)
e: e — and (= modern y) · also aver — I have (1st sg. present, apocopated form of he, perfect auxiliary: Espeso e el oro, 'I have spent the gold')
mano: mano — hand (sg.); en vuestra mano = 'in your keeping'
dixo: dezir — he/she said (strong preterite; x = sh-sound; = dijo)
sea: seer — may be, that is (present subjunctive 3rd sg.)
si: si — if; si + subjunctive alone = 'if only …!'
sobre: sobre — upon, over; here 'on the security of' (sobre aquellas arcas)
vidas: Vidas — the other of the two Jewish moneylenders of Burgos, partner of Raquel
martín: Martín (Antolínez) — a knight of Burgos, companion of the Cid, who provisions him on his exile and negotiates the loan from Raquel and Vidas
antolínez: Antolínez — surname of Martín Antolínez, the Burgalese knight who aids the Cid
burgos: Burgos — Burgos, chief city of Old Castile
todo: todo — all, every (de todo conducho, 'with every kind of provision')
recabdo: recabdo — care, precaution, strict order (= recaudo)
un: uno — a, one (apocopated masc. before a noun)
marcos: marco — mark (a unit of weight for silver, pl.)
gelos: ge + los — them to him (ge, ancestor of modern se, + los; = se los)
ovo: aver — he had (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = hubo; here perfect auxiliary, ovo bastidos = 'he had furnished')
odredes: oír — you will hear (future 2nd pl., old -edes ending; = oiréis; the minstrel's aside to his listeners)
manos: mano — hand (pl.); dar las manos = the handclasp that makes an agreement binding
burgalés: burgalés — a man of Burgos (noun/adj.; el Burgalés, an epithet of Martín Antolínez)
contado: contar — renowned, esteemed (past part. used as a standing epithet of the Campeador)
aguisado: guisar — fitting, reasonable (past part. used as adj.; variant of guisado)
parado: parar — settled, arranged (past part.; el pleyto a parado = 'has settled the agreement')
arlançón: Arlançón — the Arlanzón, the river of Burgos
vino: vino — wine (noun); also venir — he came (strong preterite 3rd sg.; por en vino a aquesto, 'that is how he came to this pass')
ora: hora — hour (= hora); en buen ora, part of the poem's honorific birth-formula, 'born in a good hour'
algo: algo — something; the poem's discreet word for money, wealth
campeador: Campeador — the Battler, the Champion (the Cid's epithet, from campo 'field of battle')
he: aver — I have (1st sg. present; perfect auxiliary, = he, and the auxiliary of the split future, e.g. doblar vos he)
ganados: ganar — gained, earned (past part. masc. pl., agreeing with its object, as with ovo bastidos; avien ganados = habían ganado)
coger: coger — to take in, shelter (here = acoger)
i: e/i — and (variant of e before some sounds) · also i — there, therein (adverb, Latin ibi, like French y; meted i las fedes, 'put your pledged faith into it')
cante: cantar — may crow, may sing (present subjunctive 3rd sg.)
gallo: gallo — cock, rooster; ante que cante el gallo, 'before the cock crows'
huebos: huebos — need (Latin opus); huebos (me) ser/aver = 'to have need (of)'
çerca: çerca — near; here adverbial, çerca o tarde = 'sooner or later' (= cerca)
santa: santo — Saint (fem.); Santa María, the cathedral of Burgos
maría: María — Mary; Santa María, the cathedral of Burgos
diestra: diestro — right, on the right side (fem.)
tí: tú — thee (stressed object pronoun; = ti, old accentuation)
tierra: tierra — land, country; one's own land
vertudes: vertud — power, virtue (= virtud; sus vertudes santas 'his holy powers')
d: de — of, with (elided form of de before a vowel, d'arena = de arena)
ira: ira — wrath; en ira del rey = to be formally cast into the king's disgrace and exile, a legal idiom, not a mere figure of speech
vala: valer — may he avail, protect (present subjunctive; vos vala 'may he keep you')
exida: exida — going out, departure (= salida; Latin exire)
noch: noche — night (apocopated form of noche; cf. anoch)
fore: seer — it may be (future subjunctive 3rd sg. of ser; = fuere)
al: a + el — to the; al menos 'even the least'
pienssan: pensar — they think; pensar de + inf. 'to set about (doing)' (epic formula)
aguijar: aguijar — to spur (one's horse), ride hard
commo: commo — as, like (spelling variant of como)
m: me — me, to me (elided form of me before a vowel, querer m'a = me querrá)
seré: seer — I shall be (future 1st sg. of ser)
convusco: con + vusco — with you (fused form; cf. con vusco, v. 75)
quanto: quanto — as much as, whatever (= cuanto)
so: so/su — his, her, its (unstressed possessive sg.; so çervicio = su servicio); also seer — I am (1st sg. present; = soy; so ayrado, 'I am in [the king's] ira')
